bounded_slice.target: Cargo source replacement using a vendored directory source and the exact network/registry claim
observations: The official page defines source replacement as redirecting communication with registries or git repositories to another data source, including an exact local copy.
It explicitly lists vendoring as a strategy where a custom source represents crates on the local filesystem and can be checked into a package.
Its configuration example defines a directory source at vendor and replaces crates-io with that local source using replace-with.
The same page notes that some commands that need direct registry contact still require --registry, so the page does not establish a universal no-network guarantee for every Cargo command.
bounded_slice.verified_scope: For dependency source replacement, Cargo officially supports redirecting the crates.io source to a vendored local directory source via .cargo/config.toml, so registry-backed dependency source retrieval can be replaced by checked-in local content for the replaced source.
bounded_slice.not_verified_scope: A universal guarantee that dependency resolution/build performs no network access for any reason; behavior of every command; Chat-native Cargo process execution; end-to-end richer-mode parity.
bounded_slice.scope_guard: Do not upgrade source replacement to a universal offline guarantee. The official page supports local replacement of dependency sources, but explicit no-network operation remains a separate condition to verify.

exact_continuation: On the next invocation, fresh-bootstrap and freeze current authority, then inspect exactly one official Cargo documentation page that directly defines --offline or equivalent no-network behavior for dependency resolution/build. Determine whether combining source replacement with that documented mode closes the network-access subclaim without broadening to actual Cargo execution; persist exact support or the remaining blocker.
